chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Do not touch the hair or the nails of the deceased, and if anything falls off from him, place it in his shroud.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on cutting or touching the hair and nails of the deceased in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi underscores the reverence for the deceased's natural state, prohibiting the cutting of hair or nails to preserve the integrity of the body as it was in life. It further instructs that any naturally shed hair or nails must be retained within the kaffan (burial shroud), reflecting the Shia emphasis on completeness and respect during the preparation for burial.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Do not touch from the deceased, neither hair nor a nail, and if something falls off from him, so make it to be in his shroud’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Nothing of the hairs or nails of a deceased is touched and if any of such things fall off, you must place them in his shroud.’”
